Each integer must contain ASCII digits only, with no signs, separators, or internal whitespace, and must be at most `100000`. Return `(width, height)` as integers. Non-string input raises `TypeError`; all malformed, zero, negative, or out-of-range forms raise `ValueError`. The input is immutable and no aliases are retained. Known-bad source:

import re

_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^\\s*([0-9_]+)\\s*x\\s*([0-9_]+)\\s*$")


def parse_canvas_size(text):
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError("text must be a string")
    match = _PATTERN.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError("invalid canvas size")
    width = int(match.group(1).replace("_", ""))
    height = int(match.group(2).replace("_", ""))
    if width <= 0 or height <= 0 or width > 100000 or height > 100000:
        raise ValueError("canvas size is out of range")
    return width, height
